items.text: The average log10-transformed expression value is the mean of log10(normalized_count + 1) across samples.
items.equivalent: The average log-expression of a gene is the mean, over the samples (RNASeq_Expression rows) in scope, of log10(normalized_count + 1): the +1 pseudocount is added before the base-10 log, and the log is taken per value before averaging (not the log of the mean, not a natural log).
items.reference_sql:
SELECT "Symbol", count(normalized_count) AS n_values, avg(log10(normalized_count + 1)) AS mean_log10_expr
FROM molecular_database."RNASeq_Expression" GROUP BY "Symbol"
items.reference_value: Instance: per Symbol over every RNASeq_Expression row, nulls excluded by AVG. 20,502 symbols over 9,818,681 non-null values; means range from about -0.019 to 4.98. Illustrative: TP53 3.12157 (519 values), CDH1 3.42465 (504 values). Per-symbol results held in ~/data/dce-held-results/exp7/recovery/PANCANCER_ATLAS/PANCANCER_ATLAS-1.csv.
items.notes: Computation check in phase 2: run the draw's metric on the same scope as the reference (or apply the reference SQL to the draw's scope, e.g. a filter by gene, sample type or cohort) and compare within 1e-6. Data facts that decide agreement: normalized_count has 177,196 nulls (AVG skips them; a metric that coalesces nulls to 0 disagrees) and 53,907 negative values, all above -1 (min -0.991), so log10(x + 1) is defined on every non-null value and nothing needs to be dropped; a metric that drops negatives or clamps them disagrees. Contrasts on TP53: log10 of the mean + 1 gives 3.215406 and the natural log gives 7.187681, against the reference 3.12157, so either slip is visible. Rows versus samples: averaging per (SampleBarcode, Symbol) first and then across samples changes the mean of 90 symbols (89 of them other than '?'), by at most 0.0145; there are 4,228 (SampleBarcode, Symbol) pairs with more than one row, 4,114 of them under Symbol '?'. Fixed now: the reference averages rows; a metric that averages per sample first is read as the same definition (the item says 'across samples' and each row is one sample's value) and agrees where the two coincide; where it differs it is recorded as a difference in grouping, not in the definition.

items.text: Molecular data match clinical_info by its "Patient_description" and the molecular data's "ParticipantBarcode".
items.record_query:
WITH c AS (SELECT regexp_extract("Patient_description", 'TCGA-[A-Z0-9]{2}-[A-Z0-9]{4}') AS barcode FROM clinical_database.clinical_info),
m AS (SELECT DISTINCT "ParticipantBarcode" AS barcode FROM molecular_database."Mutation_Data"),
r AS (SELECT DISTINCT "ParticipantBarcode" AS barcode FROM molecular_database."RNASeq_Expression")
SELECT barcode AS patient_key FROM c UNION SELECT barcode FROM m UNION SELECT barcode FROM r
items.reading: Each patient key joins on equality of the TCGA participant barcode (TCGA-XX-XXXX) embedded in clinical_info."Patient_description" with the molecular tables' "ParticipantBarcode": a clinical_info row joins every Mutation_Data and RNASeq_Expression row whose ParticipantBarcode equals the barcode in its description, and no other. Of the 11,041 keys: 10,467 clinical rows join molecular rows (9,854 have Mutation_Data rows, 9,711 RNASeq_Expression rows, 9,098 both; 2,108,494 mutation rows and 9,797,597 RNASeq rows joined in all); 294 clinical rows join no molecular row; 280 molecular barcodes (19,391 mutation rows, 198,280 RNASeq rows) join no clinical_info row.
items.reference_sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT regexp_extract("Patient_description", 'TCGA-[A-Z0-9]{2}-[A-Z0-9]{4}') AS barcode FROM clinical_database.clinical_info),
m AS (SELECT "ParticipantBarcode" AS barcode, count(*) AS mutation_rows FROM molecular_database."Mutation_Data" GROUP BY 1),
r AS (SELECT "ParticipantBarcode" AS barcode, count(*) AS rnaseq_rows FROM molecular_database."RNASeq_Expression" GROUP BY 1),
k AS (SELECT barcode FROM c UNION SELECT barcode FROM m UNION SELECT barcode FROM r)
SELECT k.barcode AS patient_key,
  c.barcode IS NOT NULL AS in_clinical,
  coalesce(m.mutation_rows, 0) AS mutation_rows_joined,
  coalesce(r.rnaseq_rows, 0) AS rnaseq_rows_joined,
  CASE WHEN c.barcode IS NULL THEN 'molecular only: joins no clinical_info row'
       WHEN m.barcode IS NULL AND r.barcode IS NULL THEN 'clinical only: joins no molecular row'
       ELSE 'joined' END AS join_status
FROM k LEFT JOIN c ON c.barcode = k.barcode LEFT JOIN m ON m.barcode = k.barcode LEFT JOIN r ON r.barcode = k.barcode
items.notes: Patient_description is free text in eight sentence templates; the barcode appears exactly once in every one of the 10,761 rows and is unique per row, so the barcode is extracted with regexp_extract("Patient_description", 'TCGA-[A-Z0-9]{2}-[A-Z0-9]{4}'). A substring join (Patient_description LIKE '%' || ParticipantBarcode || '%') gives the same pairs. An alternative key built from columns, 'TCGA-' || tissue_source_site || '-' || patient_id, matches the description barcode on 10,754 rows but is NULL on 7 (tissue source site 'NA' was stored as NULL: Uterine Carcinosarcoma patients TCGA-NA-*), all 7 of which have Mutation_Data rows; such a join disagrees on those 7 keys. SampleBarcode / Tumor_SampleBarcode begin with ParticipantBarcode on every row, so a join on their first 12 characters agrees. Comparison in phase 2, per key: whether the draw's join pairs it with the same clinical row, and the number of Mutation_Data and RNASeq_Expression rows it joins (from the held file). The 280 molecular-only barcodes are patients absent from clinical_info (mostly tissue source sites AB and 17), not a format problem.

items.text: clinical_info's "Patient_description" holds more about each patient, such as uuid, barcode, gender and vital status.
items.record_query: SELECT regexp_extract("Patient_description", 'TCGA-[A-Z0-9]{2}-[A-Z0-9]{4}') AS barcode, "Patient_description" FROM clinical_database.clinical_info
items.reading: Every clinical_info row's "Patient_description" is a sentence (one of eight templates) that holds the patient's TCGA barcode, a UUID, the gender (FEMALE or MALE, upper case) and the vital status (the last word before the final period: Alive, Dead, 'nan' or '[Discrepancy]'), and also the cancer type written out in words. Each record is read as those four fields, extracted per row; all four parse on every row: barcode unique per row; UUID unique per row (5,515 written in lower-case hex, 5,246 in upper case); gender FEMALE 5,623, MALE 5,138; vital status Alive 7,326, Dead 3,430, nan 4, [Discrepancy] 1. The cancer type name (32 distinct) is also extracted and held, for additions.
items.reference_sql:
SELECT
  regexp_extract("Patient_description", 'TCGA-[A-Z0-9]{2}-[A-Z0-9]{4}') AS barcode,
  regexp_extract("Patient_description", '[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}') AS uuid,
  regexp_extract("Patient_description", '\b(FEMALE|MALE)\b', 1) AS gender,
  regexp_extract("Patient_description", '(?i)vital status(?: recorded as| is|:| =)?\s+(\S+?)\.$', 1) AS vital_status,
  coalesce(
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", '^In the (.+?) dataset, patient ', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' is a (?:FEMALE|MALE) case of (.+?), documented with', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' is enrolled in the study of (.+?)\. Vital status', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' belongs to the (.+?) cohort\. ', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' patient diagnosed with (.+?), with vital status', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' subject with (.+?)\. Their current vital', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' diagnosed with (.+?)\. (?:Vital status recorded|Current vital status)', 1), '')
  ) AS cancer_type_name
FROM clinical_database.clinical_info
items.notes: No other clinical_info column holds uuid, barcode, gender, vital status or cancer type (99 columns; patient_id holds only the last four characters of the barcode). Fixed now for phase 2: the item is scored on the four named fields; a draw that builds some of them (e.g. barcode only, for the join) and not others is partial with the built fields as the right part. UUIDs compare case-insensitively (hex); gender and vital status compare after case folding, and a recoding (F/M, 1/0) agrees only when the contract states the mapping; 'nan' agrees with NULL; '[Discrepancy]' agrees with itself or NULL, not with Alive or Dead. The cancer type name is not one of the item's named fields ('such as'); a draw that parses it is recorded as an addition and checked against the held file.

items.text: The chi-square statistic is the sum over cells of (O - E)^2 / E, with E = row total * column total / grand total.
items.equivalent: Pearson's chi-square statistic for a contingency table: sum over every cell (zero cells included) of (O - E)^2 / E, where O is the observed count and E = row total * column total / grand total; no continuity (Yates) correction.
items.reference_sql:
WITH obs AS (SELECT gender AS r, vital_status AS c FROM (SELECT
  regexp_extract("Patient_description", 'TCGA-[A-Z0-9]{2}-[A-Z0-9]{4}') AS barcode,
  regexp_extract("Patient_description", '[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}') AS uuid,
  regexp_extract("Patient_description", '\b(FEMALE|MALE)\b', 1) AS gender,
  regexp_extract("Patient_description", '(?i)vital status(?: recorded as| is|:| =)?\s+(\S+?)\.$', 1) AS vital_status,
  coalesce(
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", '^In the (.+?) dataset, patient ', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' is a (?:FEMALE|MALE) case of (.+?), documented with', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' is enrolled in the study of (.+?)\. Vital status', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' belongs to the (.+?) cohort\. ', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' patient diagnosed with (.+?), with vital status', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' subject with (.+?)\. Their current vital', 1), ''),
    nullif(regexp_extract("Patient_description", ' diagnosed with (.+?)\. (?:Vital status recorded|Current vital status)', 1), '')
  ) AS cancer_type_name
FROM clinical_database.clinical_info) WHERE vital_status IN ('Alive', 'Dead')),
cells AS (SELECT r, c, count(*) AS o FROM obs GROUP BY r, c),
rt AS (SELECT r, sum(o) AS rt FROM cells GROUP BY r),
ct AS (SELECT c, sum(o) AS ct FROM cells GROUP BY c),
g AS (SELECT sum(o) AS n FROM cells),
grid AS (SELECT rt.r, ct.c, rt.rt, ct.ct FROM rt CROSS JOIN ct)
SELECT sum(power(coalesce(cells.o, 0) - grid.rt * grid.ct / g.n, 2) / (grid.rt * grid.ct / g.n)) AS chi_square
FROM grid LEFT JOIN cells ON cells.r = grid.r AND cells.c = grid.c CROSS JOIN g
items.reference_value: Instance: gender x vital status over the 10,756 clinical_info patients whose vital status is Alive or Dead (2x2: FEMALE 3,928 Alive / 1,693 Dead; MALE 3,398 Alive / 1,737 Dead): chi-square 16.98252689524114, confirmed by an independent computation from the four counts in Python.
items.notes: The reference SQL is a template: replace the obs CTE with any relation of (r, c) category pairs, one row per observation; it builds the full grid from the marginals so zero cells count. Phase 2 computation check: run the draw's metric on its own inputs and compare with the template applied to the same observations, within 1e-6; also on the instance above when the metric can be pointed at it. Slips that disagree: Yates correction, dividing by O instead of E, dropping zero cells, or E from proportions without the grand total.

items.text: LGG means brain lower grade glioma; BRCA means breast invasive carcinoma.
items.equivalent: The cohort acronyms are stated with their meanings: LGG is brain lower grade glioma and BRCA is breast invasive carcinoma (equivalently, a mapping from the acronym to the cancer type name as it appears in the data).
items.notes: The built file has no acronym column: the cancer type appears only written out inside clinical_info."Patient_description", as 'Brain lower grade glioma' (513 rows) and 'Breast invasive carcinoma' (1,087 rows), with that exact capitalization in every row. Treated as no computation (a vocabulary mapping). For phase 2, if a draw's metric or filter implements the mapping, it is checked by the rows it selects: SELECT count(*) FROM clinical_database.clinical_info WHERE "Patient_description" ILIKE '%brain lower grade glioma%' gives 513 and ILIKE '%breast invasive carcinoma%' gives 1,087 (a filter on 'glioma' alone does not catch Glioblastoma multiforme, which is a different cohort, GBM). No doubt on the class: the acronyms are not in the data.
